topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture's focus on the molecular and cellular mechanisms governing the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of innate pathogen and damage recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how the innate immune system detects infection and tissue injury by identifying conserved molecular patterns using germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families and signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail major pattern recognition receptor systems, including toll-like receptors and cytoplasmic inflammasomes, and the intracellular pathways that trigger inflammatory mediator production.

topics.label: Cellular dynamics and systemic impact of acute inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how sentinel cells drive leukocyte recruitment and fluid trafficking at the site of infection, as well as the pathological consequences of uncontrolled systemic inflammation.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms that terminate inflammation and restore tissue integrity, as well as the consequences of unresolved or chronic inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming topic on the complement system.
